summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by chronic marginal (gastrojejunal) ulcer and post-bypass hypoglycemia requiring continuous gastrostomy tube feeds was admitted for acute-on-chronic left upper quadrant abdominal pain localized near the G-tube site and worsened with tube feed infusion. Evaluation showed stable vital signs, reassuring abdominal exam without peritonitis, normal laboratory studies, and a chest radiograph without free air; there was no evidence of tube-site infection. Bariatric surgery recommended no additional imaging or surgical intervention, and the pain was felt most consistent with her known marginal ulcer and/or local tube-site irritation. She received IV analgesia initially, continued ulcer therapy with lansoprazole and sucralfate via tube, and tube feeds were restarted without difficulty to prevent hypoglycemia (supported with dextrose-containing IV fluids while feeds were off). Symptoms improved with pain control, and she was discharged home ambulatory with liquid oxycodone as needed and instructions to follow up with pain management and keep her planned end-of-month EGD.
problems: Chronic gastrojejunal ulcer without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
Unspecified disorder of pancreatic internal secretion
Personal history of Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus
